title: ENG-205 Beowulf Part 2 — 2 Names
subject: ENG-205
topic: Beowulf Part 2 (Another Attack to Another Celebration at Heorot)

cards.def: Grendel's mother is a monstrous water-hag descended from Cain who lives in the mere and attacks Heorot to avenge her son.
Grendel's mother kills in Heorot to take revenge for her son's death, obeying the same law of feud that human warriors follow.
Aeschere was Hrothgar's most trusted counselor and battle companion, whom Grendel's mother carried off and killed.
Yrmenlaf is Aeschere's younger brother.
Hrothgar grieves for Aeschere, describes the haunted mere, and promises Beowulf treasure if he will settle the new feud.
After the mere fight, Hrothgar speaks as a wise old king who warns Beowulf against pride.
Beowulf vows revenge for Aeschere, dives into the mere, kills Grendel's mother with a giant's sword, and returns with Grendel's head.
Unferth, once Beowulf's mocker, lends him the sword Hrunting but loses fame because he dares not fight underwater himself.
Beowulf finds Grendel's corpse in the underwater hall and cuts off its head to repay all his killings.
Heremod was a Danish king who grew bloodthirsty, killed his own companions, and stopped giving rings, so Hrothgar holds him up as a warning.
The giants were an ancient race who fought against God and were destroyed in the flood, and their story is engraved on the sword hilt.
The poet repeats that Cain's murder of Abel produced the race of misbegotten spirits to which Grendel and his mother belong.
Beowulf's Geat companions keep waiting at the mere after the Danes give up, hoping to see their lord again.
Hrothgar's Danes see blood rising in the water, decide that Beowulf is dead, and go home.
Beowulf asks that Hygelac receive his treasures if he dies, and he says Hygelac would back him in helping the Danes.
Hrethric is Hrothgar's son, whom Beowulf invites to visit the Geats' court.
The mere is full of serpents and sea-dragons, one of which Beowulf shoots with an arrow before the Danes haul it ashore.
The mere is a haunted lake near Heorot, ringed by frost-stiff woods, where the water burns at night and no hunted stag will enter.
Grendel's mother lives in a dry, firelit hall under the mere, where the roof keeps the water out.
Hrothgar says Beowulf has joined the Geats and the Danes in a pact of friendship in spite of their old hatreds.
